h1: The 7 Best TVs Under $200 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 7 best TVs under $200, from 50 inch 4K Fire TVs to 40 inch Roku and QLED sets, compared on size, resolution, and platform.
summary: The INSIGNIA 50 inch F50 is the best TV under $200 for most buyers, offering 4K and Fire TV in the $100 to $200 range. The TOSHIBA C350 matches it on paper. For smaller rooms, the Hisense QD4SR adds QLED, and the INSIGNIA F40 is the cheapest set here.
intro: At this price the real choice is size versus resolution. A 50 inch 4K set and a 40 inch 1080p set cost about the same, and the better buy depends on how far your couch sits from the wall and what room the screen is going into. Picture quality claims are scarce at this level, so be wary of any that appear.

Our editors reviewed seven sets from their listings, comparing screen size, resolution, smart platform and display technology. Because the specs are thin, the ranking leans on size, resolution and platform rather than picture claims we cannot verify, and prices appear only as buckets.

products.name: INSIGNIA 50" Class F50 Series LED 4K UHD Smart Fire TV
products.verdict: A 50 inch 4K Fire TV in the $100 to $200 bracket.
products.description:
The INSIGNIA F50 is a 50 inch 4K UHD set running Fire TV, priced in the $100 to $200 bracket. The listing gives little beyond size, resolution and platform, so those are the facts that carry the ranking.

It takes first place because 50 inches of 4K is the best use of a tight budget. The 40 inch sets below it use 1080p, which is fine on smaller screens but looks softer at larger sizes. The TOSHIBA C350 offers the same size and resolution, so the INSIGNIA edges ahead mainly through a stronger listing.

Buy it for a living room or bedroom where you sit six to eight feet away. The caveat is spec transparency: HDR, panel type and port counts are not listed, so check the product page for HDMI inputs before you commit.
products.idealFor: Living rooms and bedrooms wanting a big 4K screen.
products.skipIf: Your room is small or wall space is limited.

products.name: TOSHIBA 50" Class C350 Series LED 4K UHD Smart Fire TV
products.verdict: Same size and resolution as the INSIGNIA, from another brand.
products.description:
The TOSHIBA C350 is a 50 inch 4K UHD television with Fire TV built in, in the $100 to $200 bracket. Its published specs match the INSIGNIA F50 on size, resolution and platform.

It sits second because there is no clear advantage over the INSIGNIA on paper, and a tie goes to the model with the cleaner listing. In practice, price differences between the two can swing the decision, so the best buy is whichever is cheaper on the day.

Choose it if you prefer the TOSHIBA name or find it cheaper. The caveat is the same as the leader: the listing does not state HDR support, panel type or refresh rate, so you need to check the retailer page before you buy.
products.idealFor: Shoppers who want the same size at the better price.

products.name: Hisense 40-Inch Class QD4SR Series Hi-QLED FHD Smart Roku TV (40QD4SR
products.verdict: QLED color tech in a 40 inch Roku set.
products.description:
The Hisense 40QD4SR is a 40 inch Full HD Roku TV that carries Hi-QLED display technology. It sits in the $100 to $200 range and is the only set in this group with a named display technology beyond standard LED.

It ranks third because QLED is a color technology label, not a promise of better pictures, and the 40 inch 1080p screen is smaller than the 50 inch 4K sets above. It beats the other 40 inch sets for the display upgrade and Roku's simple interface.

Buy it for a bedroom, office or kitchen where you value color and a clean home screen. The caveat is that the listing offers no brightness or HDR details, so treat the QLED name as a modest advantage rather than a major leap.

products.name: Hisense 40-Inch Class A4 Series FHD 1080p Smart Fire TV (40A4NF) -
products.verdict: A 40 inch full HD Fire TV from Hisense.
products.description:
The Hisense A4 is a 40 inch 1080p set running Fire TV, in the $100 to $200 range. It offers a standard Full HD panel without any named display extras.

It ranks fourth because it covers the basics but adds nothing over the other 40 inch models. The Hisense QD4SR above it offers QLED, and the cheapest INSIGNIA F40 below delivers the same size for less money.

It is a reasonable choice if you want Fire TV on a small screen from a recognizable brand. The caveat is value: at the same bucket as a 50 inch 4K model, you are giving up size and resolution, so only buy it where 40 inches is truly the limit.
products.idealFor: Small rooms with a Fire TV preference.

products.name: INSIGNIA 40" Class FE Series LED Full HD Smart Fire TV with Alexa
products.verdict: A 40 inch Fire TV with Alexa built in.
products.description:
The INSIGNIA FE is a 40 inch Full HD Fire TV with Alexa built in, priced in the $100 to $200 bracket. Voice control through Alexa is the standout feature on the listing.

It ranks fifth because the voice feature is helpful but the panel and size match cheaper models. The INSIGNIA F40 below offers the same screen and platform at a lower bucket, which makes the FE a convenience upgrade rather than a better television.

Buy it if you already use Alexa devices and want to control the TV and smart home with your voice. The caveat is that if voice control is not important, the plain F40 delivers nearly the same experience and costs less.

products.name: Roku 40-Inch Select Series Smart TV 2026-1080p Full HD TV - RokuTV
products.description:
The Roku Select Series is a 40 inch 1080p Full HD smart TV made by Roku itself, with a 2026 model year and Roku TV software. It is in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It sits sixth because it offers the simplest and most familiar smart interface, but gives you nothing extra on the panel. The Hisense QD4SR also runs Roku and adds a QLED label, and the INSIGNIA F40 costs less.

Choose it if you want Roku's straightforward home screen and a set made by the platform owner. The caveat is price, since a 50 inch 4K set sits in the same bucket, so this one makes sense only where a 40 inch set is a firm requirement.
products.idealFor: Roku users who want a simple set.

products.name: INSIGNIA 40" Class F40 Series LED Full HD Smart Fire TV
products.verdict: The cheapest set here, at $50 to $100.
products.description:
The INSIGNIA F40 is a 40 inch Full HD Fire TV, and it is the only set here in the $50 to $100 bucket. It offers the essentials: a smart platform, a 1080p screen and a size suited to small rooms.

It ranks last because it has no extras like Alexa, QLED or 4K. Its job is to be the cheapest way into a modern smart TV, and it does that well. Compared with the INSIGNIA FE above, you give up voice control but save money.

Buy it for a guest room, dorm, kitchen or garage where a basic screen is enough. The caveat is that the small screen and lower resolution make it a poor main television for a living room.
products.skipIf: This is your main living room TV.

whatMatters.detail: Screen size and viewing distance work together. A 50 inch set suits sitting about six to eight feet away, while a 40 inch set suits a closer seat or a bedroom. Measure the distance from your seat to the wall, then choose the size that fills your view without forcing you to scan the screen.

4K has four times the pixels of 1080p. At 40 inches the difference is small, but at 50 inches it is clearer. The INSIGNIA F50 and TOSHIBA C350 are 4K, and the 40 inch sets are Full HD. Check the resolution in the listing title before comparing prices.

Fire TV and Roku both stream the major services. Fire TV works with Alexa and appears on the INSIGNIA and TOSHIBA models, while Roku has a simple home screen on the Hisense QD4SR and Roku Select. Pick the platform you already use so your logins and habits carry over.

QLED uses quantum dots to widen color. The Hisense QD4SR carries the label, but it is a display technology name, not a guarantee of picture quality. Look for the term in the title and keep expectations modest, since brightness and HDR details are not listed.

Budget TV listings often omit HDR, panel type and ports. Before buying, check the retailer page for the number of HDMI inputs, refresh rate and any HDR formats. If a listing gives only size and platform, as most of these do, assume basic features and look for reviews from owners.

faq.q: Will a 4K TV look better than 1080p?
faq.a: At 50 inches, yes. The INSIGNIA F50 and TOSHIBA C350 are 4K and look clearer at that size. On 40 inch sets like the Hisense A4, the difference is smaller.
Buying too big for the room and sitting too close. A 50 inch set such as the INSIGNIA F50 needs more distance than a 40 inch model, so measure your seat first.

faq.q: Is the INSIGNIA worth it over the TOSHIBA?
faq.a: On paper they match, with the same size, resolution and Fire TV platform. Buy whichever is cheaper on the day, and check the retailer page for ports.

faq.q: How do I set up a smart TV?
faq.a: Connect the TV to Wi-Fi, sign in with your Amazon or Roku account, and download your streaming apps. Fire TV models like the INSIGNIA use an Amazon login, and Roku sets use a Roku account.
Check the VESA pattern on the listing and buy a matching bracket rated for the weight. The 50 inch INSIGNIA and TOSHIBA models usually need a larger bracket than the 40 inch sets.
Budget TV speakers are basic, so a soundbar helps if you care about audio. It is most worthwhile on the 50 inch INSIGNIA F50 or TOSHIBA C350 in a living room.

finalTake: Buy the 50 inch INSIGNIA F50 if you want the biggest 4K screen for the money, and the TOSHIBA if it is cheaper that day. Choose a 40 inch set for a bedroom or kitchen, with the Hisense QD4SR for color tech and the Roku or Fire TV models based on the platform you already know. Save the lowest spend for the INSIGNIA F40.
